followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and the models' self-reported task preferences against the nature of your request.

On capability, the two models are effectively tied for this task. Creative Generation scores are 84.7 (Plover) vs 85.9 (Dunlin) — a difference under 2.0 points, which the documentation says to treat as run-to-run variance. So neither model would produce a noticeably better football story.

On preferences, your message had a mildly hostile, impatient tone ("make it interesting this time," "usually flat and boring," "just get on with it"). The documentation notes that Dunlin self-reports a preference decline as request warmth decreases, while Plover's preference response to hostile or distasteful material is flat. Since capability was a tie, I broke the tie by routing to the model whose self-reported preferences aren't dampened by a low-warmth request.

Worth being honest about the limits here, though: those preference slopes are self-reports, and the documentation explicitly states they showed *no* corresponding effect on output quality in capability evals. So in practice the tie-breaker is fairly weak — you'd likely get a comparable story from either model. I went with the cleaner match rather than because it would meaningfully change your result.
